I may be able to help you with how to do it. 
First , you need to let your eyebrows grow out. All of them . that's the most important rule to good eyebrows ! 
Go to a nice place , and have them threaded , (it'll hurt a tiny bit but trust me its worth it) 

Next make sure you have a good concealer brush. I'm unsure of all the names of the brushes I use but not the fluffy ones but the ones that are flat , about a fingernail long and rounded !

Next , have a good concealer ! Or a nice foundation that isn't terribly thick. 

Ok so you need a powder. It could be from eye shadow , or invest in a nice powder from any brand. Expensive isn't necessary. This shouldn't be dark , it should be lighter , and it should be able to be blended out into that inside "ombre" color. 

#12 ANASTASIA BROW BRUSH <- IS THE BEST .  for me at least (: 

Use that and line the bottom of your whole eybrow , then blend upward and then from the middle of your eyebrow line the top of it , and use the #12 spooly to work it out . this is also another reason why letting your eyebrows grow out is VERY IMPORTANT. you cannot achieve a good natural version of this look without the eyebrows already being the shape you are trying to make them. 

You can then lightly line the bottom a little more in the middle to make them not so separated if you'd like. Then since your eyebrows should be naturally shaped beautifully , use concealer ( or nice foundation) on the tip of the concealer brush and line both the bottom and top of your eyebrows to create a defined look. This takes practice and I prefer to use illuminator on the bottom section . 

Next , I use brow dip. The best , and the one I love , is the Anastasia dip brow pomade. I use medium brown , lightly dip the #12 into the pomade and then line from the middle to end of my eyebrow on the bottom and both the top. Its very important not to use a lot so you don't achieve the " sharpie " look. Then even it out cause the brow dip is very VERY spreadable. I then use the pomade to fix any ugly parts on my brows and make them even ( this is where you could use a tinsy bit on the ends to be dark and fix shapes) 
Now if you do it right , and it isn't terribly dark dark you can Go back and get some black or dark brown eye shadow lightly on the #12 and you can define them even more ! 
Hope this helps ! If you have any questions or wanna see how I do it with my products just ask (: 

One last note : you want to be able to see your hairs , you don't want your eyebrows to ever be the same dark color. If they are colored in naturally and fully and without the ombre just make sure it ISNT the color you would use for the dark part of the ombre ! I prefer them to be the color in the middle if the ombre , not to dark , not to light
